title: The container orchestrator must not dispatch claude workers
description:
OPERATOR CONSTRAINT, 2026-09-22: 'don't use claude on the orchestrator'.

hn0 shipped the container orchestrator using the compiled-in profiles/ - executor local-subprocess, runner claude, model sonnet - and the boot REFUSES any run whose model is not on the Anthropic route, because the claude CLI speaks the Anthropic API. So today the container can only dispatch claude workers, which is the opposite of what is wanted.

Every cloud run before hn0 used GLM 5.3 through pi on Workers AI. hn0 changed the worker model without that being a decision anyone made: the profile was chosen because it was the local-subprocess one that happened to exist.

What is needed: the container dispatches workers on the gateway-backed model the factory already pays for, NOT claude. That means a runner that speaks whatever route the gateway serves - pi is the existing one - running as a local subprocess inside the container rather than in a herdr pane.

The obstacle is real and should be stated: ticfac implements only two executors, local-subprocess and herdr. profiles-herdr/ pairs pi with herdr, and there is no herdr server in the container. So the work is to run the pi runner UNDER local-subprocess, or to establish why that cannot be done.

Check internal/runconfig/kinds.go for what each runner kind requires, and internal/exec/subprocess for what the local executor can launch. The claude-specific pieces hn0 added - the Anthropic-route refusal, IS_SANDBOX for the root permission check - are claude's requirements and should move or go with it.

Until this lands, do not start a cloud epic run: the only thing the container can currently dispatch is the thing the operator has said not to use.
notes:
2026-09-22 13:41 - OPERATOR DECISION, 2026-09-22, and this is the target rather than a preference:

  Workers run GLM 5.3 or GLM 5.3 Flash. Nothing else. Via Pi, which has a Cloudflare Workers AI adapter.

So the shape is: runner = pi, model = cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3 (or the Flash variant), executor = local-subprocess, inside the orchestrator container. That is profiles-herdr/'s ROUTING with profiles/'s EXECUTOR - neither existing profile as-is.

What this repo already knows, and what has to change:

  - profiles-herdr/ already pairs pi with cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3. That is the routing to keep.
  - It pairs it with executor herdr, and there is no herdr server in the container. That is the part to replace with local-subprocess.
  - .tick/runners.toml's [roles.implement] says implementation runs 'entirely on GLM on cloudflare through pi', so this is the repo's stated intent, not a new direction. hn0 diverged from it by taking the compiled-in claude profile.

Things hn0 added that belong to claude and should go with it:
  - the boot's refusal of any non-Anthropic route ('ticfac dispatches its workers through the claude CLI, which speaks the Anthropic API'). Under pi that refusal is backwards: it would reject exactly the route we want.
  - IS_SANDBOX=1, which exists because the claude CLI refuses bypassPermissions under root. Check whether pi has an equivalent check before removing it.
  - ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is what common.sh exports for the claude route; pi on Workers AI needs the gateway's workers-ai route instead. internal/exec/subprocess/grade.go's modelCredentialPrefixes preserves ANTHROPIC_* through the source grade - confirm the equivalent holds for whatever pi reads.

Open question to settle first, because it decides the size of this: can the pi runner be launched by the local-subprocess executor at all? internal/runconfig/kinds.go defines what each kind needs; internal/exec/subprocess is what would launch it. If pi assumes a herdr pane for its I/O, that assumption is the work.
2026-09-22 13:41 - OPERATOR CORRECTION, 2026-09-22, and it overrides hn0's executor choice:

  'the orchestrator should deploy cloudflare workers, one per parallel tick'

So the target is NOT workers as subprocesses sharing the orchestrator's container. It is one Cloudflare sandbox per tick, each running pi + GLM 5.3 / GLM 5.3 Flash - which is what docs/design/cloud-factory.md specified all along ('Worker agents | One Sandbox per tick | Minutes | Yes - ephemeral by design').

hn0 chose local-subprocess because runstate.Executors reserves the NAME 'cloudflare-sandbox' but internal/exec/ implements only herdr and subprocess. That gap is now the work rather than a reason to route around it.

The design question this raises, which I flagged during yoh's planning and never resolved: a container cannot create a sibling sandbox directly - the Sandbox binding is a Worker binding. So the executor has to ask the factory over HTTP: orchestrator container -> a Worker endpoint -> Sandbox DO -> pi/GLM worker. Containers can make outbound requests, so the leg exists.

Worth establishing before building:
  - The OLD cloud design already spawned per-tick worker sandboxes from the Run Workflow, so the sandbox-creation machinery probably exists on the Worker side; find it before writing a new one. Look for the worker/ticks-worker entrypoint (image/worker.sh) and whatever created its sandbox.
  - t5p persisted the sandbox handle so an attempt survives a Workflow restart. An executor that returns a HANDLE rather than a finished attempt is exactly what yoh's 'nothing waits' principle needs, and t5p suggests the durable half is already there.
  - Attempt identity and adoption must work across this boundary: a restarted orchestrator has to recognise a sandbox that is still running its tick, by identity, rather than dispatching a second one.
  - Isolation and cost change: one sandbox per tick instead of four processes in one container. max_instances is 3 today, and the dispatch width has its own copy of that number in wrangler.toml - both bound how wide a wave can be.
2026-09-22 15:15 - THE WORKER SIDE LARGELY EXISTS - FIND IT BEFORE WRITING IT (checked 2026-09-22).

cloudflare/src/sandbox-executor.ts is 724 lines of exactly the machinery this tick
needs: namedSandbox(binding, name) resolves a Sandbox DO by name, findWorkProcess
inspects a running one, and the module is built around NOT carrying a live Sandbox
object across a step boundary - which is the same handle-not-a-result discipline yoh
needs and t5p persisted.

Its only caller is epic-reconciler.ts:1649 via sandboxExecutorFromEnv, and mn7 deletes
that caller. So the work is smaller than 'implement a cloudflare-sandbox executor':

  Worker side  - give sandbox-executor.ts an HTTP entry point instead of an
                 in-isolate caller.
  Go side      - internal/exec/ gains a third executor beside herdr and subprocess
                 that speaks to that endpoint and returns a HANDLE, not a finished
                 attempt.
  Identity     - adoption must recognise a sandbox still running its tick across the
                 restart boundary, by identity, rather than dispatching a second one.

Sequencing that follows from this: xte should land BEFORE mn7, or mn7 should leave
sandbox-executor.ts alone. A note on mn7 says so.
acceptance_criteria: A cloud epic run dispatches each tick into its OWN Cloudflare sandbox running pi on GLM 5.3 or GLM 5.3 Flash, and starts NO claude process anywhere in the container for ANY role, review and closeout included; no worker shares the orchestrator's container; a role with no cloud routing declared refuses the run at start rather than falling back to a default; the orchestrator survives a restart without dispatching a second sandbox for a tick already running one; proven by a run whose trace shows the expected provider per attempt.
closed_reason: merged as building blocks in #33 (operator's choice B); its unmet goal lives in yoh (xev, gbs, a08, nwn, 6gr)
